title: Reattach your detached wrist camera
instruction: Reattach the loose camera to its mount on your left wrist. Release it once it is secured.
setup: Fixed bimanual YAM station: rigid metal arms with parallel grippers, bases (0,+0.305,0.750) and (0,-0.305,0.750) m, initial joints [0,1,1,-0.6,0,0] rad and open grippers. Wooden tabletop 1.10x1.30x0.06 m, centre (0.36,0,0.7175) m, top z=0.7475 m. Rigid polymer camera housing 40x36x28 mm,55 g, spawned at (0.36,-0.19,0.7725) m with identity body rotation and allowed to settle; front lens on +Y. Rear polymer shoe nominally20x4x24 mm; aluminium channel with20.4 mm internal width, retaining lips, stop, two7 mm-square supports, and a spring-loaded retaining tooth with a mechanically coupled side push button and a tapered shoe nose. Exact part dimensions in mechanism_dimensions.json; original optical target in native_camera_target.json. Apple66 mm/120 g at XY(0.30,0.28), orange64 mm/110 g at XY(0.40,0.26); natural fruit mesh appearance, rigid contact, mesh bottoms placed on table. Station floor, lighting and metal top-camera stand:110x110x16 mm foot,12 mm radius mast,9 mm radius arm,50x42x22 mm camera housing; calibrated transforms and lengths in the pinned environment. Top and right wrist feeds remain available; left feed follows detached housing. Fruit is context only. All materials describe physical counterparts; rigid fruit and an elastic, connected USB cable. The custom wrist receiver and camera plate are permanently screw-fastened to their respective assemblies; the recoverable connection is the keyed plate-to-receiver interface.
scoring: 0.25: housing-and-plate reference box >20 mm above table for1 s, closing gripper command and TCP within50 mm of envelope; pickup credit persists unless invalidated. 0.5: optical position error <=5 mm and rotation error <=5 degrees for1 s while held or latched. 0.75: verified entry through channel, seating and current latch engagement with alignment maintained. 1.0: aligned latched camera and advancing camera frame delivery persist2 s after other TCP is >80 mm from envelope. Alignment/release intervals reset when interrupted. Below-table drop (body z < tabletop-50 mm) invalidates all credit. No READY-return condition. Sensor/housing consistency is diagnostic, not scored. The reference box is X[-20,20],Y[-27,18],Z[-24,14] mm in the camera body frame; the USB plug, boot and flexible cable are excluded from lift/proximity checks.
fidelity: A keyed camera plate, tapered guide mouth, retaining lips, end stop and spring tooth provide contact-driven retention. A left-side push button and rigid rear return yoke retract the tooth mechanically. The connected USB cable uses a capsule chain with elastic D6 joints. The original optical target is unchanged.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.00; scripted demo: 1.0. Current cable-connected push-button adapter; model limit1800 control steps.
context: Restore the robot’s own displaced wrist-camera module to its original sensing configuration. The camera remains connected to the arm by a flexible USB cable; the other arm must retrieve and install it on the receiving wrist’s quick-release adapter. The receiving arm can reposition its mount to enable insertion. This combines handling a cable-tethered module with coordinating insertion and released retention on the robot itself, targeting automation of robot hardware setup and maintenance.
reset_notes: A fresh process restores the fixed scene, robot initial joints, detached camera and spring plunger. For mechanical removal, support the camera, press the side button inward to retract the tooth, then slide the camera out of the guide.
